text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- General Workers' Union calls for cost-of-living wage rise. Union presents proposals to Finance Minister Spiteri as he prepares budget expected in parliament in mid-January.
- Housing Authority to spend $17 million on social housing next year; figure is slightly higher than this year's.

- VAT erodes Enemalta's profits; state-owned energy corporation made profit of Lm1.7 million after tax in financial year to September last year compared to Lm12 million the previous year; substantial amount of fall in profits came about after corporation absorbed VAT instead of charging consumers.
- General Workers' Union says it is ready to help new government as long as workers' rights are unaffected.

- Government abandons plans to build administrative centre on controversial site; previous government had been considering building centre on site of popular soccer pitch just outside capital, Valletta.
- Government revenue up 2.8 percent in first 10 months of this year, but deficit widened owing to greater recurrent expenditure, Central Office of Statistics says.
